name: Aalborg
title: Aalborg Ship Gauging: UTM for Cement Carriers and Bulk Ships
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Aalborg for cement carriers, bulk carriers, feeders and tankers on the Limfjord: holds, ballast tanks and deck plating.
h1: Thickness Measurement for Cement Carriers and Bulk Ships at the Port of Aalborg
intro: Aalborg is North Jutland's main port, reached from the Kattegat along the Limfjord. Its quays serve a cement industry that ships its product far beyond Scandinavia, along with bulk carriers moving grain, feed, fertiliser and coal, container feeders, small tankers and general cargo ships. Cement and bulk cargoes are hard on holds, ballast tanks and discharge gear, which is why superintendents often want readings during an Aalborg call. For each job, Atlantis mobilises a technician team from India to the ship and works alongside while she loads or discharges.

highlights.p: Aalborg Portland's works at Rørdal, east of the city, ships grey and white cement from its own harbour. Cement carriers making repeated loading calls develop wear in their discharge pipework, hold structure and ballast tanks, all worth measuring at regular intervals.

highlights.h: Abrasive bulk over the public quays
highlights.p: Grain, feed, fertiliser and coal cross the port's bulk quays. Grab damage, abrasion and damp residues take metal off hold frames, lower brackets and tank-top plating, so these areas lead the scope when a bulk carrier is gauged between hatches.

highlights.h: A fjord port with its own limits
highlights.p: The approach along the Limfjord follows a dredged, buoyed channel, and ships bound further west must pass the city's opening bridges. Draught, wind-driven water levels and, in hard winters, ice decide sailing times, so gauging windows follow the pilot's plan.

p: The Limfjord cuts across the north of Jutland from the Kattegat to the North Sea, and Aalborg stands at its narrowest point, with Nørresundby on the opposite shore. Ships arrive from the east, entering the fjord at Hals and following a dredged channel inland towards the city. The port's main commercial quays and the industrial harbours lie east of the centre, so most cargo ships berth without passing the road and railway bridges that cross the fjord at Aalborg; vessels bound for berths further west, or for the smaller Limfjord ports, go through the opening spans by arrangement. Tidal range is small, but water levels in the fjord respond to the wind, and a strong blow from the west or east can change the depth available in the channel for a day or two.

Industry built the port. Aalborg Portland's large cement works at Rørdal exports cement by sea from its own harbour, including white cement that goes to markets far from Denmark. The coal-fired power station has its own quay for fuel deliveries, and the public port handles grain, feed, fertiliser, coal, oil products and building materials, together with project cargo and a container terminal that now concentrates on companies in North Jutland after the Greenland base traffic moved away at the end of 2022. Container feeders link the port with the North Sea hubs. Short-sea bulk carriers, cement carriers, small tankers, general cargo ships and feeders make up most of the traffic, and the bulk of the ships calling here are short-sea tonnage sized for the fjord rather than deep-sea giants.

Cargo patterns are seasonal. Grain and feed shipments follow the harvest and the livestock trade, fertiliser imports build ahead of spring, and coal movements have shrunk as Danish power generation has moved away from coal, leaving the bulk quays with spells of heavy activity and quieter weeks between them. Cement loads steadily through the year. Winters are usually open, but the Limfjord is shallow and sheltered, and in a severe cold spell ice can form in the fjord and slow traffic until icebreaking or milder weather clears it. The ships that trade into the fjord regularly are often small, older vessels on repeated voyages, and constant loading of abrasive cargoes with frequent ballasting is exactly the service that thins hold and tank structure.

facilities.h: Where ships are gauged at Aalborg
p: Aalborg is a cargo port rather than a repair port, so gauging is done afloat at the berth where the ship works cargo. At the cement harbour, a carrier loading has her holds in use, but she pumps out ballast as the cargo comes aboard, so emptied and ventilated ballast tanks, the deck, the discharge system's pipework and the machinery spaces form the scope. At the public bulk quays, holds can be measured one by one as grab discharge empties them, before the next cargo goes in, while a ship loading there frees her ballast tanks instead. Tankers at the oil berths keep their cargo tanks closed throughout, leaving deck structure and segregated ballast as the realistic targets.

For dockings, ships trading to Aalborg usually go to Ørskov Yard in Frederikshavn, a short passage north up the Kattegat, to Fayard on Funen, or to yards in Poland and the Baltic states, depending on size and the owner's habits. Superintendents often use an Aalborg call shortly before a docking to measure the holds and tanks most likely to need steel, then send that estimate to the yard so the work can be planned before the ship arrives. Ships idle at the port while waiting for cargo or between charters are the best candidates for pre-purchase and condition gauging, because nothing else competes for access to the spaces.
list: Aalborg Portland's cement harbour, Rørdal — ballast tank, deck and discharge-pipework gauging on cement carriers during loading.
Public bulk quays — hold frames, lower brackets and tank-top plating measured on bulk carriers hold by hold during discharge.
Oil and liquid bulk berths — deck and segregated ballast tank readings on small product tankers, with cargo tanks left closed.
Container terminal — deck, hatch coaming and ballast tank measurement on feeders, following the terminal's crane sequence.
Waiting berths — pre-purchase and condition gauging on ships lying idle between cargoes or charters.
Ørskov Yard, Frederikshavn — the nearest repair yard for shell and bottom gauging when an Aalborg trader goes to dock.

context.h: Port state control, abrasive cargoes and fleet age at Aalborg
p: The Danish Maritime Authority carries out Paris MoU port state control at Aalborg, where much of the traffic is older short-sea tonnage that the risk profile pushes towards more frequent inspection. Structural findings on these ships tend to be predictable: wasted hatch coamings and hatch cover skirt plates, holed air pipes and ventilators on deck, corrosion of hold frames and their brackets, and thinning in the ballast tanks behind them. Each can end in a requirement to measure and repair, and a gauging scope agreed in advance can turn a detention risk into a planned repair at the next convenient yard.

Cement carriers are a specialised fleet with a wear pattern of their own. Many are converted bulk carriers or purpose-built self-dischargers, and their pneumatic or mechanical discharge systems push abrasive powder through pipes, bends and pumps that wear from the inside. Cement dust settles on decks and in voids, and in damp air it holds moisture against the steel. Owners of this tonnage also face the EU ETS (from 2024) and FuelEU Maritime (from 2025) on voyages to and from Danish ports, plus the Inventory of Hazardous Materials that ships of 500 GT and above need when calling in the EU, and both push them to review which ageing ships justify another renewal survey.

jobs.h: Gauging work that Aalborg calls generate
jobs.p: Most requests from Aalborg concern holds, ballast tanks and deck on ships that carry abrasive or damp cargoes. A superintendent typically asks for a defined group of spaces to be measured while cargo is worked, either to follow up corrosion recorded at the last survey or to build a steel estimate before a docking. Cement carriers add their discharge pipework to the list. The scope is fitted to the time alongside and to the order in which holds and tanks become free, and readings go to the ship and the office as each space is completed, so repair decisions can be taken before the ship sails back down the fjord. Common jobs include:
list: Ballast tank and discharge-line gauging on a self-discharging cement carrier loading at Rørdal, ahead of her intermediate survey.
Hold frame and tank-top measurement on a short-sea bulk carrier discharging grain, after a surveyor recorded wastage at the lower brackets.
Hatch coaming and air-pipe readings on a general cargo ship following a port state control deficiency at the previous port.
Pre-docking gauging of ballast tanks on a container feeder before she docks at Ørskov Yard.
Pre-purchase gauging of holds and ballast tanks on a coaster lying idle at a waiting berth.

logistics: Aalborg Airport, on the north side of the fjord, has international connections and lies a short drive from the port, while Copenhagen and Billund airports are the long-haul alternatives, linked to Aalborg by rail and domestic flights. The public quays are ISPS-controlled and access is arranged through the ship's agent, whereas the cement works and the power station run private harbours with site inductions and access rules of their own. The team travels from India on Schengen visas, and we fix travel once the agent confirms the ship's arrival in the fjord.

faqs.q: Can cement carrier discharge pipework be measured at Aalborg?
faqs.a: Yes, when the system is shut down and the master's permit system allows it. Pneumatic discharge lines wear fastest at bends, reducers and wherever the flow changes direction, so readings concentrate there, with a grid of points on each bend. Results are set out against nominal wall thickness with sketches of each run, which lets the owner decide which spools to renew at the next yard stay.

faqs.q: Does ice in the Limfjord affect inspection work in winter?
faqs.a: Only in severe winters, when ice can slow traffic in the shallow fjord and delay arrivals. In most years the fjord stays open and work continues normally. When a hard cold spell is forecast, we keep in touch with the agent about the ship's expected arrival and adjust the team's travel, because a delayed berthing shortens the time available alongside.

faqs.q: Can bulk carrier holds be gauged during grain discharge at Aalborg?
faqs.a: Often, hold by hold. Once a hold has been emptied and swept and the stevedores have moved on, the team can measure frames, brackets and tank-top plating before the hatch is closed or the next cargo arrives. Access, lighting and the use of the ship's own ladders are agreed with the chief officer, and the order follows the discharge plan rather than the numbering on the TM plan.

faqs.q: Where do Aalborg traders dock, and can the readings go with them?
faqs.a: Usually at Ørskov Yard in Frederikshavn, at Fayard on Funen, or at a Polish or Baltic yard. Readings taken in Aalborg are referenced to the TM plan's frames and strakes, so the yard and the attending surveyor can use them to plan steel renewal and the close-up survey. If the owner wishes, the team can also travel on to the yard to complete the shell and bottom readings with the ship dry.
